ltm-en.json — vendored, verbatim, never edited by hand.

  package   long-term-memory 1.2.9
  repo      Marinara-Agents @ d9b93fe
  path      the package client's en locale bundle
  sha256    ead6a546372bf1af688e3655ffa4960bb8827a2158219b85651f652d188f7b6e
  entries   1171 keys (1078 distinct normalised strings)

Why it is here and not under src/tools/memory/: it is the whole console's
vocabulary, not the memory tool's. Every area's copy file resolves its
`use` pointers into this table, so it sits beside them in src/copy/.

Refreshing it is a two-step change, never one:
  1. copy the new file in, update the version/commit/sha above
     (`shasum -a 256 src/copy/vendor/ltm-en.json`);
  2. run `node design/copycheck.mjs`. A `use` pointing at a key the new
     bundle dropped is a fatal integrity failure, and a console coinage the
     new bundle has since grown a word for is also fatal. Both are the
     point: an upstream release is exactly when our coinages go stale.

Do not reformat it. Byte-identical to upstream is what makes the sha useful.
